sources.supports: August 2027 arrival, Phobos proximity operations from September, sampling in 2030, return in 2031. No precise insertion day/time claimed.

sources.supports: Approximate 27 × 22 × 18 km dimensions; irregular cratered body.

sources.title: JPL planetary satellite mean elements
sources.supports: Phobos semimajor axis about 9,375 km from Mars center; displayed rounded to ~9,400 km, not altitude.

sources.title: ISAS News 537, December 2025, p.6
sources.supports: Driven double-tube corer and sample retention; sampling at two different locations on Phobos.

sources.title: JPL Horizons spacecraft −239 / archived local planning states
sources.supports: JAXA 20261019_20281231_MMX_V0.2 planning solution; outbound geometry through 2027-08-29 04:57 UTC. The following planning-arc discontinuity is not a resolved capture burn.

scope_notes: All dates are planned; no flight reconstruction or official-service claim.
19 October UTC and 20 October JST are the same scheduled launch event.
Return is stated at year precision; no July 2031 claim.
At least 10 g is the total mission return target, not a promise from each sampler.
Two techniques are not assigned one-to-one to two fixed sites.
QSO sketch is relative motion near Phobos; both bodies orbit Mars.
No original JAXA/ESA image pixels or agency logos are incorporated.
